title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 376
paragraphs: When Psammis had been king of Egypt for only six years and had made an expedition to Ethiopia, and immediately afterwards ended his life, Apries son of Psammis inherited the kingdom in succession. This man came to be the most prosperous of all the kings up to that time, except only his forefather Psammetichos, and he reigned twenty-five years, during which he led an army against Sidon and fought a sea-battle with the king of Tyre. Since, however, it was fated that evil should come upon him, it came through a matter which I shall relate at greater length in the Libyan history, and only briefly here. Apries sent a great expedition against the Kyrenians and met with a correspondingly great disaster; and the Egyptians, considering him to blame for this, revolted against him, supposing that Apries had deliberately sent them out to obvious ruin so that — as they said — there might be a slaughter of them and he might the more securely rule over the rest of the Egyptians. Indignant at this, both the men who had returned from the expedition and the friends of those who had perished openly revolted.
